settings.headline: About Larkmoor College
settings.subtitle: A fictional residential college of liberal arts and sciences on the Calder River, built to show what a college website looks like on Raytha.

settings.headline: Small classes, real projects, a river at the door
settings.body:
In this story, Larkmoor College was founded in 1891 as a teachers' seminary and grew into a college of six schools. About 3,400 undergraduates and a small graduate program study on a 180-acre campus between the old quad and the Calder River.

Programs · Faculty · Campus · News

items.title: A seminary on the river
items.text: Larkmoor opens in Thornbury Hall with 42 students training to be teachers.

items.title: Becoming a college
items.text: The seminary becomes Larkmoor College and adds degrees in the sciences and humanities.

items.title: Hollis Library opens
items.text: A new library gives the growing college room for its collections and its students.

items.title: The arts get a home
items.text: The Marlowe Arts Center opens with a concert hall, a black box theater and studios.

items.title: Science on the river
items.text: The Calder Science Center opens, with a rooftop greenhouse and a river research station.

items.a: No. Larkmoor College, its people, buildings and teams are fictional. Any resemblance to a real institution is accidental.
It is a Raytha use case: a full college website built on an open-source .NET CMS, with a kit you can rebuild yourself.

items.q: Where do the images come from?
items.a: Every illustration, portrait and PDF was generated by a script, so nothing here is a photo of a real place or person.
